It provides end-to-end operational oversight, maintaining real-time visibility of incidents, risks, and performance to support timely decision-making and service continuity. The position is responsible for coordinating incident triage, prioritisation, and escalation across multiple resolver teams and service providers, while supporting Major Incident Management processes and acting as a key escalation point for high-impact issues. It also oversees workforce planning and roster management to ensure continuous operational coverage and seamless service delivery. Through strong governance and adherence to IT service management practices, the role ensures consistent execution of processes, maintains operational standards, and drives service performance across both Command Centre and Service Desk functions. It works closely with internal teams, service delivery managers, and vendors to enable coordinated, cross-functional service delivery. The role contributes to continuous improvement by analysing operational data, identifying trends and risks, and implementing enhancements to service processes, performance, and resilience. Through leadership and stakeholder engagement, it ensures the delivery of reliable, responsive, and customer-focused operational services aligned with organisational priorities.

review_candidates.title: Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) – Insurance & Investments
review_candidates.description: 1. Role Summary The Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) is responsible for leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives to improve organizational performance, operational efficiency, business agility, and long-term competitiveness across the insurance and investment businesses. The role involves developing and executing the organization's transformation strategy, modernizing business models, optimizing operating structures, driving digital adoption, and leading strategic change programs. The CTO will work closely with the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team to translate corporate strategy into measurable transformation outcomes. The ideal candidate will combine strategic leadership, financial and operational expertise, technology awareness, and strong change management capabilities, with a proven track record of delivering complex transformation initiatives in insurance, investment management, banking, or financial services. 2. Key Responsibilities Enterprise Transformation Strategy Develop and execute the organization's enterprise-wide transformation strategy and roadmap. Identify opportunities to improve business performance, operational effectiveness, profitability, and organizational agility. Align transformation priorities with corporate strategy, market conditions, and long-term business objectives. Evaluate existing business models, organizational structures, and operating processes to identify improvement opportunities. Establish transformation objectives, milestones, governance frameworks, and measurable success criteria. Business Model & Operating Model Transformation Lead initiatives to modernize business models, operating structures, and service delivery frameworks. Drive organizational restructuring, process redesign, and business integration initiatives. Improve operational efficiency across insurance underwriting, claims, policy administration, distribution, and customer service. Support transformation of investment operations, portfolio reporting, client servicing, and wealth management processes, where applicable. Develop scalable operating models to support business expansion, diversification, and organizational growth. Digital & Technology Transformation Lead technology-enabled business transformation initiatives in collaboration with the CIO, CTO, and CDO. Drive adoption of automation, AI, advanced analytics, cloud solutions, and digital platforms. Modernize legacy systems, enterprise applications, and operational infrastructure. Oversee transformation programs involving InsurTech, FinTech, digital insurance, and investment platforms. Ensure technology investments deliver measurable improvements in productivity, customer experience, and business performance. Financial & Operational Performance Improvement Identify opportunities to improve profitability, reduce operating costs, and optimize resource utilization. Lead cost transformation, process efficiency, and productivity improvement programs. Establish performance management frameworks and operational KPIs. Evaluate transformation business cases, financial benefits, investment requirements, and expected returns. Monitor cost savings, revenue improvements, and overall financial impact of transformation initiatives. Organizational Change Management Develop and implement change management strategies to support enterprise transformation. Build organizational readiness and secure leadership and employee engagement. Lead communication, training, and stakeholder engagement initiatives during transformation programs. Address resistance to change and promote a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement. Support leadership development and workforce transformation initiatives. Customer & Business Experience Transformation Drive initiatives to improve customer journeys and service delivery across insurance and investment businesses. Collaborate with the Chief Experience Officer and commercial leadership to improve customer satisfaction, retention, and engagement. Simplify customer onboarding, claims processing, policy renewals, investment transactions, and client servicing. Promote customer-centric operating models and consistent service standards. Use customer insights and analytics to identify transformation priorities. Risk, Governance & Regulatory Transformation Ensure transformation initiatives align with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and corporate governance requirements. Work with risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit teams to strengthen organizational controls. Lead initiatives to improve regulatory reporting, risk management processes, and governance frameworks. Assess transformation-related operational, financial, technology, and regulatory risks. Establish appropriate controls and accountability throughout transformation programs. Strategic Projects, M&A & Business Integration Oversee major strategic transformation programs, including mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, and post-merger integration. Lead integration of business processes, systems, teams, and organizational structures following acquisitions. Support new market entry, geographic expansion, and business diversification initiatives. Coordinate cross-functional transformation projects involving multiple subsidiaries and business units. Track project outcomes and ensure delivery of expected strategic and financial benefits. Leadership & Stakeholder Management Work closely with the CEO, Board, executive team, and business unit heads to establish transformation priorities. Lead transformation offices, program directors, project managers, and cross-functional teams. Establish transformation governance, reporting structures, and performance accountability. Manage relationships with external consultants, technology partners, and implementation specialists. Present transformation progress, business impact, risks, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and the Board. 3. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field. MBA or Master's degree in Business Strategy, Organizational Development, Finance, or Transformation Management preferred. 12–15+ years of progressive experience in corporate strategy, business transformation, management consulting, operational excellence, or enterprise change management. At least 5 years in a senior executive or leadership role overseeing large-scale transformation initiatives. Significant experience in insurance, banking, investment management, asset management, wealth management, or financial services. Proven track record of leading complex enterprise transformation programs with measurable financial and operational outcomes. Strong understanding of insurance operations, investment services, financial products, and regulated business environments. Experience in operating model redesign, organizational restructuring, digital transformation, and process optimization. Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business performance management capabilities. Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management skills. Preferred Certifications: Prosci Change Management Certification. Certified Business Transformation Professional (CBTP). PMP or Program Management Professional (PgMP). Lean Six Sigma Black Belt. Agile or Scrum certifications. 4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Achievement of enterprise transformation milestones. Cost savings and operational efficiency improvements. Revenue growth and profitability improvements resulting from transformation. Reduction in process turnaround times and operational bottlenecks. Successful implementation of new operating models and business processes. Digital adoption and automation rates. Customer satisfaction and service delivery improvements. Employee engagement and organizational change adoption. Successful integration of acquired businesses and strategic partnerships. Realization of expected transformation benefits and ROI. Regulatory compliance and risk management effectiveness. Delivery of transformation initiatives within approved budgets and timelines.

review_candidates.title: Chief Operating Officer
review_candidates.description: Scion Executive Search has been retained to conduct an immediate search for the Chief Operating Officer (COO) of WomenHeart , a national nonprofit dedicated to improving the lives of women living with or at risk for heart disease while championing equity in heart health outcomes. This is a full-time, remote position, with preference given to candidates located on the East Coast. About Womenheart Since 1999, WomenHeart: The National Coalition for Women with Heart Disease has been the nation's only patient-centered organization solely dedicated to advancing women's heart health through support, education, advocacy, and community. Founded by women living with heart disease, WomenHeart has built a powerful national network that connects patients, caregivers, clinicians, and advocates around a shared mission: helping women live longer, healthier lives while addressing persistent inequities in cardiovascular care and outcomes. Over the past 25 years, WomenHeart has become a leading voice in women's cardiovascular health, establishing the only national network of patient support groups, training more than 1,000 women heart disease survivors as community educators in partnership with Mayo Clinic, launching impactful advocacy and health equity initiatives, and reaching hundreds of thousands of women through educational programs such as the Red Bag of Courage®. As the organization enters its next phase of growth and influence, WomenHeart is expanding its leadership team to strengthen operational excellence, scale its impact, and advance meaningful change in women's heart health nationwide. This is an exciting opportunity to join a mission-driven organization at a defining moment in its evolution. As WomenHeart enters its next phase of growth, the Chief Operating Officer will play a critical role in strengthening organizational effectiveness, expanding impact, and advancing a vision in which every woman has equitable access to the support, education, and care needed to thrive. Position Overview The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a key member of WomenHeart's executive leadership team and a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer. As the organization enters its next phase of growth and influence, the COO will play a pivotal role in translating vision into action, strengthening organizational capacity, and driving operational excellence across the enterprise. Serving as WomenHeart's senior operational leader and chief integrator, the COO will align people, processes, resources, and priorities to advance the organization's mission and achieve measurable impact. The COO will ensure that strategic and operational decisions are informed by meaningful data, organizational realities, and long-term sustainability considerations. This leader will be adept at synthesizing complex organizational, financial, programmatic, fundraising, and volunteer engagement information into actionable insights that support executive leadership and Board decision-making. The COO will strengthen organizational effectiveness, foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement, and build the systems, infrastructure, and leadership practices necessary to support a growing organization powered by staff, volunteers, advocates, and partners. Success in this role will require an accomplished leader who can build alignment across diverse stakeholder groups, lead through influence, and cultivate strong partnerships in support of WomenHeart's mission. The ideal candidate will bring experience scaling organizational capacity and navigating periods of growth, complexity, and transformation. While not directly responsible for fundraising, the COO will play a critical leadership role in creating the operational foundation necessary to support sustainable revenue growth, program expansion, and long-term organizational success. Responsibilities Execution & Organizational Performance Partner with the CEO and executive leadership team to develop and execute the organization's strategic and annual operating plans, budget, and organizational priorities. Translate strategic goals into actionable operational plans, measurable objectives, key performance indicators (KPIs), and cross-functional accountability structures. Establish and oversee organizational performance management systems, including dashboards, reporting processes, and metrics that track program impact, fundraising effectiveness, volunteer engagement, financial performance, and organizational health. Provide the CEO, leadership team, and Board with data-driven insights and recommendations that inform strategic decision-making and organizational priorities. Drive a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence across the organization. Develop and maintain enterprise risk management practices, including identifying organizational risks and implementing mitigation strategies to support long-term success. Ensure organizational communications, messaging, and stakeholder engagement efforts align with strategic priorities and mission objectives. Leadership & Cross-Functional Alignment Lead, coach, and develop functional leaders across programs, operations, communications, and future areas of organizational growth. Foster strong cross-functional collaboration, ensuring alignment around organizational priorities, resource allocation, decision-making, and execution. Clarify roles, responsibilities, and accountability structures to improve organizational effectiveness and accelerate results. Identify and address barriers to execution, collaboration, and performance while promoting a high-performing, mission-driven culture. Operations, Infrastructure & Organizational Effectiveness Provide executive oversight of operational systems, processes, technology, and administrative infrastructure to ensure organizational effectiveness, scalability, and mission impact. Lead and develop operational staff while establishing clear goals, performance expectations, and accountability measures. Oversee financial operations, including budgeting, forecasting, financial performance monitoring, audit coordination, cash flow visibility, and compliance with regulatory, board, and funder requirements. Serve as the organization's senior human resources leader, overseeing talent acquisition, onboarding, performance management, employee relations, compensation administration, compliance, professional development, and culture initiatives. Continuously evaluate and improve organizational systems, workflows, and infrastructure to enhance efficiency, effectiveness, and long-term sustainability. Partner closely with development leadership to ensure fundraising strategies are supported by strong operational systems, reporting, forecasting, and performance measurement. Strategic Partnership with the CEO & Board Serve as the CEO's primary partner on organizational execution, operational performance, and strategic implementation. Provide regular visibility into organizational progress, emerging opportunities, operational challenges, and recommended solutions. Drive follow-through on key organizational priorities and executive commitments. Partner with the CEO and Board to strengthen governance processes, prepare board materials, and support strategic oversight and decision-making. Organizational Growth & Scaling Partner with the CEO to develop and implement a multi-year operational roadmap that strengthens infrastructure, talent, technology, systems, and organizational capacity. Build and enhance the structures, processes, and operating systems necessary to support program growth, advocacy efforts, fundraising success, communications, and national impact. Represent WomenHeart in strategic partnerships and collaborative initiatives, serving as a senior leader responsible for successful implementation and execution. Advance organizational readiness for growth by strengthening governance, decision-making, accountability, and operational excellence as WomenHeart expands its reach and influence. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred. 15+ years of progressive leadership experience, including senior operations, general management, or enterprise leadership roles within nonprofit, healthcare, public health, advocacy, or similarly mission-driven organizations. Demonstrated success leading organizational growth, change, and operational excellence, with the ability to translate strategy into execution and deliver measurable results in complex environments. Strong experience using data, financial information, performance metrics, and organizational insights to drive decision-making, accountability, and continuous improvement. Proven ability to build alignment across diverse stakeholders, lead through influence, develop high-performing teams, and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and mission-driven impact. Exceptional strategic thinking, systems orientation, judgment, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable recommendations for executive leadership and Boards. Preferred Qualifications Experience serving as a COO or in a comparable senior enterprise leadership role. Experience within a nonprofit, healthcare, patient advocacy, membership, or volunteer-driven organization. Experience partnering closely with CEOs and Boards and supporting fundraising effectiveness through operational leadership. Experience leveraging technology, automation, and AI-enabled tools to improve organizational effectiveness and scalability. Compensation And Benefits This full-time, remote executive leadership opportunity offers a competitive salary of $140,000-$160,000 , commensurate with experience, and a comprehensive benefits package. While preference is given to candidates in the Washington, DC area, exceptional remote candidates with experience supporting growing nonprofit organizations and the ability to travel regularly will be considered. WomenHeart offers 100% employer-paid medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, and disability coverage for employees , a 401(k) with employer contributions, generous paid time off and holidays, a wellness benefit, and a monthly remote work stipend. Applications And Nominations WomenHeart has retained the services of Scion Executive Search, an executive search firm specializing in recruiting for mission-driven organizations, to assist in conducting this important search. Through innovative team building and recruitment solutions, Scion Executive Search seamlessly bridges the gap in interim and executive searches. Our track record and recruitment process have made us one of the top recruitment firms in the nation. We are proud to be part of the Forbes lists of the Best Recruitment Firms and the Best Executive Search Firms in America. Additionally, Scion has been recognized as a ClearlyRated Best of Staffing firm as well as a top recruitment firm by The Business Times . Additional information about our firm and our practices can be found online. We are committed to the principles of Equal Opportunity Employment and are dedicated to making employment decisions based on merit and value, for ourselves, our client companies, and the candidates we represent. For opportunities located in a region that has enacted fair chance, arrest, or conviction-based employment ordinances, Scion Executive Search proactively follows the enacted guidance and considers for employment all qualified applications with arrest and conviction records. We engage in socially conscious business practices and believe that diverse, equitable, inclusive, and non-biased talent and recruitment processes are foundational to the success of Scion as well as every client organization with whom we partner.

It also means working inside the commercial agenda: shaping new products and markets early and finding the compliant route to the outcome. This is an office-based role in Auckland. Benefits: Competitive salary and executive incentive structure A mandate to build a best-practice compliance function within a growth business Office-based in Auckland, with flexibility around international time zones when the work needs it Regional travel as required To be considered for this position, please submit your CV via the link below. For a confidential discussion, contact Daniel Turner at Hunter Campbell on 021 193 0369 or email danielt@huntercampbell.co.nz.
